description: Experiment B, SPARK half (burst, observational). The same Spark stage, inputs and code as p15-a-spark (inputs REUSED from Phase 14, planned deviation 3: J09 export run=ce46078e05b80d2d5e119939b7d04306 of D6 attempt 4 and the ER identity assignments of run:v1:23b913cc4dab1155d7a75c505eff5d56, ER attempt 20261119T020635Z-f159535e498a-5bd1), into its own new out-root graph/runs-p15-b/ATTEMPT_ID, no export. Settings that differ from p15-a-spark: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions 128 (A: 32) and managed-scaling maximum 4 core units (A: 2). Records EMR requested, provisioned (running) and released capacity over time (CoreNodesRequested, CoreNodesRunning, TotalNodes*, the instance lifecycle), YARN pending containers, records out, tasks, stages and shuffle per stage group, duration, failures and estimated cost. Compared ONLY with p15-a-spark; a run without a capacity increase is reported as 'no scale-out observed' with the series and is never re-run for that reason.
datasetSnapshot: dblp-2026-11-01 (DBLP XML with dblp.dtd), subset rule dblp-subset-v1 (datasets/dataset-manifest.yaml); Spark inputs reused from Phase 14 (J09 run=ce46078e05b80d2d5e119939b7d04306, ER run=23b913cc4dab1155d7a75c505eff5d56)

notes: APPROVAL: the human signs this exact file at D9 with the line APPROVED-MANIFEST-SHA256: HEX64 in docs/agent-runs/phase-15/approvals.md; any change is a new sha256 and a new approval. OBSERVATIONAL: B is never re-run because it did not scale out. WILL B SCALE (decision 11.6, measured in 6b with aws-api get-metric-data on the Phase 14 clusters, Maximum per 60 s): every Phase 14 EMR run at managed-scaling maximum 4 scaled out: D8 attempt 1 (Spark, 200 default partitions) requested 4 core nodes from minute 3 and ran 4 from minute 7; D8 attempt 2 (Spark, 32 partitions) requested 4 from minute 5 and ran 4 from minute 8 to its end; D9 (Spark export, 32 partitions) went 2 -> 4 and dropped to 3 and back while running; D6 attempt 4 (Hadoop) went 2 -> 4 -> 2 -> 4 -> 2 while running. So the Phase 14 record suggests B (maximum 4, 128 partitions) will request and run more than 2 core nodes, and that a managed scale-in while the cluster still runs is possible but was not seen in either D8 Spark run; that is an expectation, not a promise. EMR managed scaling adds core units when YARN has pending containers (Spark dynamic allocation asks for executors; ContainerPending above 0) and removes them when nodes are idle (EMR Management Guide, 'Using managed scaling', https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-managed-scaling.html, cited by infra-engineer 5a). A run without a capacity increase is reported as 'no scale-out observed' with the series, never as scaling. Released capacity is read as the drop of CoreNodesRunning while the cluster runs (a scale-in event, counted for the gate only if it happens before termination) or, at the end, the instance and cluster end times from describe-cluster and list-instances, labelled a lifecycle record, not a measured zero. COST (estimate): expected about $0.80 = about 40 min (Phase 14 D8 attempt 2: 32.5 min mostly at 4 core nodes; estimate) x up to 5 m5.xlarge (primary + 4 core) x $0.24 per instance-hour (COSTS.md EMR row and its Phase 15 128-partition row, estimate); costBoundUsd 2 is about twice that; upper bound from the remote limits (state machine 14,400 s + idle end 900 s at 5 instances) about $5.10 (estimate), above the runner's $5 cap, so D11b is attended and the orchestrator gives read-only status lines and, with the human's go, stop-execution if it runs well past its expected end (about 45 min after start, estimate). DURATION: maxDurationSeconds 17,400 = --wait-timeout 14,700 + cluster end wait 900 + 1,800 margin. METRICS: every EMR query seen in account (aws-api list-metrics, Phase 14 cluster j-07168191925RA7C2EGJU, 6b); TotalUnits*/CoreUnits* dropped (not published for instance-group clusters); AWS/States seen in account but shared with the overlapping p15-a-spark run. LIMITATIONS known in advance: B overlaps p15-a-spark, C and D (no shared resource except the NAT gateway and the state machine's AWS/States series); inputs made at build commit f159535e (deviation 3).
